dossier.purpose: Reference command-line implementation of the Development Containers spec (npm package @devcontainers/cli, package.json version 0.89.0, copyright Microsoft Corporation). It reads devcontainer.json and builds, starts and configures a dev container on a local Docker-compatible engine by shelling out to the docker, docker compose and buildx CLIs (README.md:3; src/spec-shutdown/dockerUtils.ts:293-345). A multi-service app is supported only by pointing devcontainer.json at user-authored Docker Compose file(s) via dockerComposeFile + service (+ runServices). Services, volumes and networks are defined in those Compose files and started with `docker compose up -d`; the CLI adds generated override files for the dev service (src/spec-node/dockerCompose.ts:420-436, 469-573). It also runs lifecycle commands, execs into the container, and has Features/Templates authoring and publishing subcommands. It has no stop/down commands (README.md:22-23).

claims.claim: The repository holds the dev container CLI, which 'can take a devcontainer.json and create and configure a dev container from it'.

A dev container 'can be used to run an application, to separate tools, libraries, or runtimes ..., and to aid in continuous integration and testing'; 'Dev containers can be run locally or remotely, in a private or public cloud'.
'This CLI is in active development.' Implemented: build, up, run-user-commands, read-configuration, exec, outdated, upgrade, features <...>, templates <...>.
`devcontainer stop` ('Stops containers') and `devcontainer down` ('Stops and deletes containers') are listed as not yet done (unchecked boxes).

Lockfiles (.devcontainer-lock.json) are generated by default on `build`/`up` 'to pin feature versions for reproducible builds'; `--no-lockfile` opts out, `--frozen-lockfile` enforces an existing lockfile.

A standalone install script downloads a bundled Node.js runtime (no pre-installed Node.js needed) and works on Linux and macOS (x64 and arm64); it supports --version, --prefix, --update and --uninstall.
npm install needs Python and C/C++ installed 'to build one of the dependencies'.

`devcontainer up --workspace-folder <path>` downloads the image from a registry and starts the container; sample output shows `docker build` / `docker run` and a one-line JSON result {outcome, containerId, remoteUser, remoteWorkspaceFolder}.
`devcontainer exec` runs a command in the container with userEnvProbe, remoteUser, remoteEnv and other properties applied.
example-usage scripts show injecting tools into a dev container, using a dev container as a CI build environment, and building an image from devcontainer.json with Features.
Build from sources with `yarn` and `yarn compile`, then check with `node devcontainer.js --help`.
The spec seeks to enrich existing formats 'while still providing a simplified, un-orchestrated single container option'.
The project is under an MIT license (LICENSE.txt).

readme.telemetry_and_network: Telemetry: none found. A case-insensitive search of the whole repo for telemetry/analytics/appinsights/phone-home returns nothing, and package.json lists no telemetry dependency (package.json:88-105). Accounts: the CLI itself needs none. Network calls found in code: (1) every `up`/`build` GETs https://containers.dev/static/devcontainer-control-manifest.json (user-agent 'devcontainers-vscode'), cached 5 min in <tmpdir>/devcontainercli[-user]/control-manifest.json, failure tolerated (src/spec-configuration/controlManifest.ts:39-93; src/spec-node/disallowedFeatures.ts:13-14; src/spec-node/configContainer.ts:64; src/spec-node/devContainersSpecCLI.ts:724). (3) api.github.com / github.com release downloads for GitHub-hosted Features, plus direct tarball URIs (containerFeaturesConfiguration.ts:930-947, 1090-1096). (4) `git clone` of --dotfiles-repository inside the container (src/spec-common/dotfiles.ts:22-77). (5) The Docker engine's own pulls and builds. (6) install.sh contacts registry.npmjs.org and nodejs.org (scripts/install.sh:259-301). HTTP honours proxy env via ProxyAgent and allows plain http with a warning (src/spec-utils/httpRequest.ts:24-31). Registry credentials come from DEVCONTAINERS_OCI_AUTH, ~/.docker/config.json (DOCKER_CONFIG) credHelpers/credsStore/auths, a platform default credential helper, or GITHUB_TOKEN for ghcr.io; otherwise access is anonymous (httpOCIRegistry.ts:288-343, 359-442). `--secrets-file` supplies env secrets to lifecycle commands and masks them in logs (devContainersSpecCLI.ts:172, 1509-1535; devContainers.ts:302-310; spec-common/injectHeadless.ts:518). OCI auth hardening is opt-in, default off (devContainersSpecCLI.ts:71-83).

entry_points.what: CLI main: yargs command registration (lines 55-120) and handlers for up/set-up/build/run-user-commands/read-configuration/outdated/upgrade/exec
launch() and createDockerParams(): probe docker, buildx, engine version and compose CLI, then resolve the container (lines 82-270)

code.architecture: A TypeScript codebase bundled by esbuild into one file (esbuild.js:62-84), split into five tsconfig sub-projects: src/spec-node (CLI + orchestration), src/spec-configuration (devcontainer.json types, Features/Templates OCI, lockfile, control manifest), src/spec-common (host exec/pty, lifecycle injection, dotfiles, variable substitution), src/spec-shutdown/dockerUtils.ts (docker/compose CLI wrapper) and src/spec-utils (log, HTTP, fs). Flow: devContainersSpecCLI.ts -> devContainers.ts (createDockerParams) -> configContainer.ts (read JSONC devcontainer.json, check disallowed Features, run initializeCommand on the host, dispatch at :69-78) -> singleContainer.ts (image/Dockerfile) or dockerCompose.ts (Compose) -> spec-common/injectHeadless.ts (lifecycle hooks, userEnvProbe, remoteEnv, dotfiles, secrets). Features: containerFeatures.ts plus spec-configuration/containerFeaturesConfiguration.ts, containerFeaturesOCI.ts and httpOCIRegistry.ts extend the image with Feature layers; imageMetadata.ts merges the `devcontainer.metadata` label. Multi-service handling: user-authored Compose files define services, volumes and networks. The CLI treats the named `service` as the dev container. It passes `runServices` to `up -d`, and with none set starts every service (dockerCompose.ts:420-430). It rewrites that service's entrypoint (sleep-loop wrapper), labels, mounts, env, caps and GPU via an override file in the persisted folder (dockerCompose.ts:469-573). It adds top-level `volumes:` entries for volume-type mounts (:569-571, 750-764) and names the project from COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, .env, compose `name:` or the folder name (:638-682). It needs `docker compose` v2 or `docker-compose` v1 (:704-731) and uses `additional_contexts` only for compose >=2.17.0 (:190-192). `up` returns composeProjectName in its JSON (devContainers.ts:90-98). Ports for Compose services must live in the compose file: `forwardPorts` is parsed but never applied, and `appPort` is applied only to single-container `docker run` as 127.0.0.1:port (singleContainer.ts:346-348). The engine is Docker by default; Podman and wslc are detected via `docker -v` (dockerUtils.ts:301-321). Containers are found by labels devcontainer.local_folder/devcontainer.config_file (singleContainer.ts:17-18) or compose project/service labels (dockerCompose.ts:24-25). Lifecycle state markers live inside the container (injectHeadless.ts:432-445). The lockfile .devcontainer-lock.json lives next to devcontainer.json (lockfile.ts:103-106).
code.packaging_and_release: Only the npm package @devcontainers/cli is released. `yarn package` runs esbuild production bundle -> patch package.json (blank dependencies/devDependencies) -> `npm pack` -> restore (package.json:23; build/patch-packagejson.js:16-19). `files` ships devcontainer.js, dist/spec-node/devContainersSpecCLI.js, scripts/updateUID.Dockerfile, README/CHANGELOG/LICENSE/ThirdPartyNotices (package.json:46-55). The CI `cli` job builds devcontainers-cli-<version>.tgz and uploads it as an artifact (.github/workflows/dev-containers.yml:16-44). Pushing a `v*` tag triggers publish-dev-containers.yml: it checks the tag equals the package.json version (optionally with -pre-release), downloads the CI TGZ for that commit via dawidd6/action-download-artifact (pinned by SHA), and runs `npm publish ${TGZ} --access public` on Node 24 with `id-token: write` (.github/workflows/publish-dev-containers.yml:3-49; CONTRIBUTING.md:28-38). No checksums, signatures, SBOM, explicit `--provenance`/attestation step, or GitHub Release asset upload appears in any workflow. The standalone installer pulls from registry.npmjs.org and nodejs.org (scripts/install.sh:259-301). Third-party notices are regenerated through Azure Pipelines component governance (azure-pipelines.yml:14-52).
code.tests_and_ci: Mocha + Chai via ts-node (package.json:40-44; .mocharc.yml, 6-minute default timeout). 37 *.test.ts files under src/test/ (plus container-features/ and container-templates/ subfolders), about 450 `it(` call sites by regex (cli.exec.base.ts is shared by 4 exec test files), and 12 compose-* fixture dirs under src/test/configs. Integration tests create real containers, need Docker (Podman for cli.podman.test.ts) and shell out to the packed .tgz (docs/contributing-code.md:8, 50, 94-104). Compose is exercised in cli.up.test.ts, cli.exec.base.ts, cli.build.test.ts and dockerComposeUtils.test.ts. Workflows: dev-containers.yml (`cli` job: yarn install --frozen-lockfile, type-check, lint with eslint --max-warnings 0, package, upload tgz; `tests-matrix`: 15 shards on ubuntu-latest with Docker + Podman + binfmt; `features-registry-compatibility`; `install-script` on ubuntu and macos; aggregate `tests` gate), test-docker-v20.yml (Docker 20.10 -> cli.up.test.ts), test-docker-v29.yml (Docker 29.0.0 -> cli.up.test.ts), test-windows.yml (windows-2022, only containerFeaturesOCI.test.ts and generateFeaturesConfig.test.ts enabled), test-plan-item-validator.yml (issue triage), publish-dev-containers.yml (release). Also azure-pipelines.yml (component governance + NOTICE generation) and weekly Dependabot for npm, github-actions and devcontainers (.github/dependabot.yml).
code.dependencies: package.json: 16 runtime `dependencies` (chalk, follow-redirects, js-yaml, jsonc-parser, ncp, node-pty, proxy-agent, pull-stream, recursive-readdir, semver, shell-quote, stream-to-pull-stream, tar, text-table, vscode-uri, yargs), 30 `devDependencies`, 1 `resolutions` entry (package.json:56-108); yarn.lock is the lockfile (CI uses `yarn install --frozen-lockfile`); engines node >=20.0.0 (package.json:17-19). External runtime tools: a docker CLI (or podman via --docker-path), `docker compose` v2 plugin or `docker-compose` v1 (src/spec-node/dockerCompose.ts:704-731), optional buildx (src/spec-shutdown/dockerUtils.ts:254-270), git (src/spec-common/git.ts:21-27), optional docker-credential-* helpers (httpOCIRegistry.ts:444-458).

ThirdPartyNotices.txt lists only permissive third-party licenses (MIT/ISC/BSD/0BSD/Python-2.0, e.g. :20, :264, :644, :2495) but lags package.json (tar 6.2.1 at ThirdPartyNotices.txt:543 vs ^7.5.10 at package.json:101).

risks: Compose lifecycle sits outside the CLI. There are no stop/down commands (README.md:22-23; src/spec-node/devContainersSpecCLI.ts:95-116) and `shutdownAction`/'stopCompose' is never acted on (src/spec-node/imageMetadata.ts:195), so containers, networks and volumes persist until removed with docker compose (the tests do exactly that: src/test/testUtils.ts:106-113). With no `runServices`, `up -d` is issued without service names, so every service in the compose files starts (src/spec-node/dockerCompose.ts:420-430).

Documentation gap and drift. Compose support is absent from the README, which only says 'un-orchestrated single container' (README.md:164). The help block omits set-up (README.md:74-86 vs devContainersSpecCLI.ts:96). The npm prerequisite note looks stale (README.md:63 vs CHANGELOG.md:303). example-usage/README.md:13 says Node.js 16 while engines require >=20 (package.json:17-19). ThirdPartyNotices.txt lags package.json (ThirdPartyNotices.txt:543 vs package.json:101). `forwardPorts` is parsed but not implemented (example-usage/README.md:50; only `appPort` is applied, single-container only: singleContainer.ts:346-348).

State durability and scope. Generated compose override files, caches and the control manifest live under <tmpdir>/devcontainercli[-user] unless --user-data-folder is given (src/spec-node/devContainers.ts:151; src/spec-node/utils.ts:644-646) and are regenerated if missing (dockerCompose.ts:373-418). Non-compose configs mount the workspace's Git root by default (devContainersSpecCLI.ts:141). The default Compose project name is built from the folder name only (dockerCompose.ts:638-682), so two checkouts with the same folder name would get the same project name (inferred from dockerCompose.ts:676-681).

Reproducibility is partial. The lockfile pins Features only (src/spec-configuration/lockfile.ts:12-46). Base images, Dockerfile FROMs and compose service images (e.g. `mongo:latest` in src/test/configs/compose-image-without-features/.devcontainer/docker-compose.yml:21) are not pinned or digest-checked by the CLI.

Remote-controlled behaviour. Every `up` and `build` fetches https://containers.dev/static/devcontainer-control-manifest.json, even when no Features are used (src/spec-node/disallowedFeatures.ts:13-14; src/spec-configuration/controlManifest.ts:39, 84-93). A listed Feature makes `up` fail and stops a running dev container (disallowedFeatures.ts:30-48). The fetch failure is tolerated, so the blocklist silently does not apply when offline (controlManifest.ts:62-75).

Host execution and credentials. `initializeCommand` from devcontainer.json runs on the host with the host environment before the container exists (src/spec-node/configContainer.ts:66; src/spec-node/utils.ts:538-622). The CLI has no trust prompt (`isTrusted` is declared but unused, utils.ts:150). Registry credentials are read from DEVCONTAINERS_OCI_AUTH, Docker config/credential helpers (incl. platform defaults) or GITHUB_TOKEN (src/spec-configuration/httpOCIRegistry.ts:288-343, 359-442). `--oci-auth-hardening` is opt-in and default false (devContainersSpecCLI.ts:71-76), so by default bearer realms named by a registry can receive its credentials (httpOCIRegistry.ts:237-262). Plain-HTTP requests are allowed with a warning (src/spec-utils/httpRequest.ts:28-31).

Release and supply chain. The release workflow publishes with `npm publish` on tag push and grants `id-token: write`, but passes no `--provenance` flag and has no checksum, signing or attestation step (.github/workflows/publish-dev-containers.yml:8-11, 48-49); no GitHub Release assets are built. install.sh, run as `curl ... | sh` from the main branch (README.md:36), downloads Node.js and the CLI tarball without integrity checks (scripts/install.sh:259-301). Most workflow actions are referenced by mutable tag (checkout@v6, setup-node@v5; publish-dev-containers.yml:18-22) with one SHA-pinned third-party action (:41). There is no SECURITY.md.

Platform and test coverage. The main test matrix runs only on ubuntu-latest (.github/workflows/dev-containers.yml:47). The Windows job enables only 2 test files (.github/workflows/test-windows.yml:26-51). Podman tests cover single-container `up` only, with no Compose-under-Podman test (src/test/cli.podman.test.ts:24-43). The Docker 20.10 and 29.0.0 jobs run only cli.up.test.ts (test-docker-v20.yml:62; test-docker-v29.yml:44). No GPU integration test exists (src/test/imageMetadata.test.ts covers metadata only). macOS is exercised only for install.sh (dev-containers.yml:145-156).
